title: canonical path-identity comparison, applied at the worktree gitdir pointer
action: Fix ONE real product bug: the worktree gitdir bidirectional identity check. Validation corrected this cell's earlier draft on four points — read them as requirements. THE SITE, and only this site: packages/bee/lib/worktree-store.mjs:1110, `if (path.resolve(reverseResolved) !== path.resolve(gitWorktreeDir)) return null;`. When the two strings denote the same directory but do not match byte-for-byte, a linked worktree fails to resolve, `bee worktree merge` never reaches its verify child, and the merge-queue suite times out waiting for a marker — that is the FAIL LOUD chain behind test_msn_invariants invariants 7 and 12. NOT A SITE: worktree-store.mjs:491 (readWorktreeGitVerifiedId) performs no comparison — it extracts an id and returns path.basename(gitdir), which IS git's registry key and must keep git's exact spelling. Canonicalizing there is a category error and case-folding there is actively harmful. Leave it alone. WHAT THE SEPARATOR STORY GETS WRONG: :1098 and :1109 already do .replace(/\\/g, path.sep) and wrap in path.resolve, and path.win32.resolve normalizes forward slashes — separators are ALREADY handled at this site. The residual delta is realpath (8.3 short-name aliasing: a runner reports C:\Users\RUNNER~1\... where the long form differs) and case. Do not 'fix separators', re-run, and declare victory. IDENTITY BY INODE IS UNSAFE AS STATED: Node reports ino = 0 on filesystems with no file index (FAT/exFAT, many SMB/UNC shares, historically directories), so two distinct directories would compare EQUAL — exactly the wrong-pointer-accepted failure this fix exists to prevent. Treat a zero inode (or a zero device) as unusable and fall back to the string comparison. Hardlinks and junctions also compare EQUAL by identity while being distinct paths, so identity is a fast path for the common case, never the only rule. CASE SENSITIVITY IS PER-VOLUME, NOT PER-PLATFORM: APFS can be either, Windows supports per-directory case sensitivity (WSL sets it), Linux can mount case-insensitive. A `process.platform === 'win32'` fold is itself the 'EQUAL for two paths that must stay distinct' bug. Detect the volume's actual behaviour — for example by probing whether the existing path resolves under a case-flipped spelling — and cache that per root rather than assuming from the platform. THE TEST SEAM, which the earlier draft left unreachable: resolveWorktreeById(mainRoot, id) has no options bag and is called internally, so a helper that is only unit-testable in isolation leaves the site itself unproven. Give the comparison an explicit injection seam AND thread it to this call site (an options parameter with a default, a module-level test hook, or an env-gated override — choose one, name it in the trace, and make the site's test drive the real resolveWorktreeById rather than the helper alone). THE VERIFY MUST DISCRIMINATE: every leg of the earlier draft's verify was green on the unmodified tree — measured by validation. Name your new test file explicitly in the verify (run_verify --only takes explicit tokens and will not pick up a new file otherwise), and record a red-first proof: with the old raw comparison restored, your new fixture fails; with the fix, it passes.

the comparison is injectable AND the injection reaches resolveWorktreeById's own call site: the site's test drives the real resolveWorktreeById, not the helper in isolation
a fixture whose pointer differs only in spelling (the case the injection simulates) resolves correctly, and a fixture with a genuinely wrong pointer still returns null
red-first evidence is recorded: with the old raw comparison restored the new fixture fails; with the fix it passes
the verify names the new test file explicitly and no existing worktree suite regresses — worktree store, merge queue and msn invariants all pass locally
the release-manifest regen chain ran inside this cell and release_manifest.mjs --check is green

Separator handling is now delegated entirely to the platform-appropriate path.resolve (injectable via platformPath, default the ambient node:path) -- win32.resolve already normalizes '/' to '\\' on its own, and posix.resolve correctly leaves a literal backslash as data. Also addressed all three advisory residuals: case-fold now requires BOTH sides to agree (not just side A), the volume-behaviour cache is keyed by device number (not ancestor path string), and the probe now prefers a read-only basename-case-flip check before ever falling back to the write-based marker probe. Test suite hygiene fixed: sibling worktree directories are now removed alongside mainRoot in every fixture.

checks.evidence: No platform branch in code — the only win32 mentions are comments. Detection is a real write-probe against the nearest existing ancestor, cached per root, with every failure path defaulting to no-fold (probe target missing, unwritable directory, concurrent rename all return false). The probe marker always contains letters so the comparison cannot degenerate. Residuals recorded as advisory: the fold is decided from side A and applied to both; the cache key is the nearest EXISTING ancestor rather than the volume, so a pair whose own parent is missing can inherit an answer probed at a different mount point; the cache is module-global and never invalidated; and the probe performs a WRITE, which on the merge path lands inside the git worktree metadata whenever the reverse pointer is stale — a comparison with a filesystem side effect.

Both fields on both sides are guarded. Forcing the zero case in scratch over two genuinely distinct directories: zero inode and device on both sides, zero inode only, zero device only, and zeros on one side only all fall back to string comparison and return unequal; the same path with zeros returns equal. The suite's own control asserts the same.

The seam is an options parameter defaulting to the real helper, threaded from the merge entry points. One fixture drives the real merge with NO injection, so the default comparison decides: it builds a directory symlink alias and rewrites the reverse pointer to that string, and the two strings are provably not already equal because reverting the site to the raw comparison makes exactly that test fail. No production caller can inject.
Byte-diff of the readWorktreeGitVerifiedId region before and after is identical (the region shifted one line from the new import). The returned basename keeps git's exact spelling.

Reproduced in scratch: reverting only the comparison line turns the suite from 9/9 to 7 passed / 2 failed, exactly as the trace records. Both failures are assertion failures carrying the unknown-id error, not compile or import errors — the other seven tests execute and pass, which proves the imports resolved.

Constructed two genuinely different, simultaneously existing directories that compare EQUAL. The helper replaces every literal backslash with the platform separator on the stated claim that a backslash is illegal in a POSIX filename — that claim is false; backslash is a legal POSIX filename character. The fold also runs BEFORE resolve and BEFORE stat, so the identity fast path stats the wrong location. On this Linux box, a directory literally named a-backslash-b compares equal to the genuinely different a/b, and the stat of the first argument was confirmed to land on a/b. True whether or not the second directory exists; identity does not rescue it. Directionally this is a NEW accept: the reverse pointer was already backslash-folded before this cell, but the other side was compared raw, so a backslash-bearing root or worktree id used to refuse and can now be accepted. Reachability at the wired site is narrow — it needs a literal backslash in the main root or the worktree id on a POSIX volume — but this is exactly the wrong-pointer-accept class the cell exists to prevent. Other probes came back clean: a symlink alias to a different directory returns false; hardlinked files share an inode and return true, which the plan's correction explicitly accepts and which cannot arise for directories; the zero-inode plus forced-fold combination needs a case-insensitive volume holding two case-differing directories, which cannot exist.

Six files, all inside the cell's declared globs, no unrelated edits. Judge's own runs: the new suite, the merge-queue suite, the msn invariants and the worktree store suite all pass, and the release manifest reports 395 files matching. Hygiene nit: the new suite removes its main root but not the sibling worktree directories, leaking four directories per run into the temp area.

semantic_judge.failure_signature: canonicalPathsEqual folds literal backslashes to the platform separator on every platform, before resolve and before stat, so on POSIX a directory literally named a-backslash-b compares EQUAL to the genuinely different a/b and the identity fast path stats the wrong location — a wrong-pointer accept newly reachable on one side of the wired comparison.

checks.evidence: Round 1's experiment re-run against the reworked module: two simultaneously-existing, genuinely distinct directories — one named with a literal backslash, one nested — now compare UNEQUAL in both argument orders, and the variant where the nested directory does not exist also returns false, while a path compared with itself still returns true. The hand-rolled fold is gone; the only separator handling is the injected platform's resolve. Win32 injection compares a backslash spelling equal to its slash form, correctly. No NEW false equal from injecting win32 on POSIX: the win32-resolved forms do not exist there, so the identity fast path throws and falls to a string comparison of two strings that are genuinely identical under win32 semantics — the fast path never stats a wrong EXISTING location. A drive letter differing only in case returns false, which is the safe direction. No production caller passes the platform injection; only tests do. Minor injection-only smell: the volume detection walks ancestors with the ambient path rather than the injected one, so under win32-on-POSIX both sides collapse to the same answer — no false equal, but the probe is meaningless in that configuration.

Reproduced read-only via a module resolve hook redirecting the helper to a scratch copy carrying the pre-rework body verbatim, leaving the tracked tree untouched: 11 passed, 2 failed — exactly the both-sides-fold guard and the POSIX backslash guard, with assertion messages rather than compile errors, and the other eleven checks executing and passing. Baseline unmodified: 13 passed. Caveat recorded: the windows-shaped fold test also passes under the pre-rework module (the old fold happened to produce the same lowercased string), so it does not discriminate the blocker on POSIX; the two named guards are the load-bearing ones, as claimed.

The case decision now requires both sides to agree. Measured in both orders on a non-existent pair: insensitive-then-sensitive returns false after two probes; sensitive-then-insensitive returns false after one, since the conjunction short-circuits and never probes the second side — outcome correct either way. Neither side inherits the other's answer. Honesty note on the test: it does not construct a real straddle; it injects a call-counter returning true then false over a pair on one device. It pins the code's contract rather than a real two-volume scenario, and a genuine straddle is unconstructible on this single-volume machine — the test's own comment says so.

The cache key is now the device number, with the ancestor path string as fallback. Failure modes probed: a throwing stat falls back to the path key and works; two different real volumes do not collide. One real collision class found and recorded as advisory: with a forced zero device, two distinct directories share the single key, the probe runs once, and the second inherits the first's answer — so every no-file-index volume reporting device zero shares one cache slot, and on such a volume the identity fast path is also unusable, leaving the poisoned fold to decide. Narrow and unreproducible on this box. A second residual in the same family: the read-only probe compares device and inode, which on a zero-identity volume evaluates zero-equals-zero twice and reports case-insensitive whenever a case-flipped sibling merely exists. The cache remains module-global and uninvalidated, which matters less with a device key than with a path key but is what makes the zero-device poisoning persist for the process.

The read-only probe runs first and the write probe is reached only on a null return, which happens in exactly two cases: no case-bearing character in the basename, or an unstat-able sample. Proved by instrumenting the filesystem write and driving the detection: probing a stale gitdir pointer under the git worktrees directory recorded NO writes, because that ancestor has letters and the read-only path settles it; probing under a numeric-basename ancestor recorded a real write. So a comparison can still write, under exactly that condition — identity unusable AND the nearest existing ancestor's basename carrying no case-bearing character. Round 1's specific concern, a write landing inside git worktree metadata on the merge path, is closed for the realistic shape.

Five files, all inside the cell's declared globs plus bookkeeping, and every code change maps to a finding: the fold removed and the platform injected (the blocker), the both-sides conjunction, the device key, the read-only probe, and the fixture cleanup. The worktree store was untouched this round. Judge's own runs: the path-identity suite 13/13, the merge-queue suite, the msn invariants and the worktree store suite all pass, and the release manifest reports 395 files matching. The herding suite's red was confirmed as wpi-2's coupling rather than a wpi-1 break: the only failing check was wpi-2's own guard row, on the single assertion that pins the removed universal backslash fold, with its six other checks green — and re-running that suite through the pre-rework hook turned it fully green, which is proof of causation.
